cafe: I usually order a flat white, but yours tasted quite bitter yesterday.
We changed the beans this week. Would you prefer a lighter roast?
Maybe. I liked the old one because it was less sharp.
I'll make you a small sample before you choose.
I'm meeting someone who doesn't drink caffeine.
Our fruit infusions are caffeine-free, although the green tea isn't.
That's useful. I nearly ordered green tea for both of us.
I'll leave the boxes here so your friend can read the ingredients.
Why is my coffee more expensive than hers? We ordered the same size.
Yours has almond milk. I should have mentioned the extra charge.
I don't mind paying, but I couldn't find it on the board.
You're right. The price needs to be beside the milk choices.
I brought a travel cup. Can you fill it to this line?
That leaves enough room for the lid, doesn't it?
Exactly. Last time the drink leaked into my bag.
I'll wipe the outside as well before handing it back.
Could you cut that slice into two smaller pieces?
Of course. Are they going on separate plates?
Yes. My son wants cake but never finishes a whole slice.
Then I'll put the cream on the side so you can share it.
This tastes of hazelnut, though I ordered vanilla.
Please don't drink any more while I check the order.
I don't have an allergy; it's just not what I wanted.
Thanks for clarifying. I'll replace it rather than add more vanilla.
Would you mind moving that bag from the empty chair?
Sorry, I was keeping the seat for my colleague.
Is she arriving soon? I'm only waiting for a takeaway.
She'll be another twenty minutes. You're welcome to sit there.
I think we've been charged for a sandwich we didn't receive.
Was it the toasted cheese one?
Yes. We cancelled it when you said the kitchen had closed.
I can see the cancellation now. I'll take it off the bill.
We need somewhere for a book group on Thursday evenings.
How many people usually come, and will you be ordering food?
Around eight, mostly drinks. We need to hear each other speak.
The back room is quieter, but we'd need a regular booking.
Your staff were lovely, but our order disappeared twice.
Were both orders placed at the counter?
One there and one through the table code.
That may explain the confusion. I'll check how those two systems connect.
travel: The cheaper ticket says I must travel after nine thirty.
My train leaves at nine twenty-eight. Does that really make a difference?
Unfortunately it does. The restriction is based on departure time.
Then I'll take the next one rather than risk paying again.
I've followed the signs, but they keep sending me round the same block.
The old bus stop signs haven't all been removed.
So the temporary stop isn't outside the station?
No, it's beside the cinema. I'll point it out from here.
My first train was cancelled, and the app wants me to buy a new ticket.
Don't buy it yet. Your existing ticket may cover the alternative route.
Even though that train belongs to a different company?
Check the disruption notice. It lists which services are accepting tickets.
Someone has taken a suitcase that looks exactly like mine.
Is the one left on the belt the same model?
Yes, but the label has a different name.
Give the desk that name. They can contact the other passenger privately.
We have forty minutes between flights, and we're still on the ground.
Have you booked both flights on the same reservation?
Yes, so I expected the connection to be possible.
Tell the airline staff now. They can check what happens if we miss it.
The bike's front light works, but the rear one doesn't.
Did you notice before leaving the hire station?
About two streets away. I've brought it straight back.
Thanks. We'll swap the bike and record the fault.
The app calls this route accessible, but it includes a long staircase.
Could it be referring only to the station entrance?
Maybe, but that isn't clear when you plan the whole journey.
I'll report the route itself, not just the broken lift.
The driver wants a separate payment for each of us.
Did we agree on two fares or one shared journey?
One journey. We gave both addresses before getting in.
Let's check the booking message before either of us pays.
The refund form asks for a ticket number I can't find.
It may be on the original confirmation rather than the payment receipt.
I only saved a screenshot of the code.
Keep that screenshot. Customer support should tell you which number they need.
Flying saves two hours, but getting to the airport adds nearly as much.
The train arrives right in the city centre too.
And we'd avoid paying for a taxi at the other end.
Once we include those costs, the train seems the better option.
hotel: Our booking is confirmed, but you say there are no rooms.
The system has your arrival down as yesterday.
The confirmation on my phone clearly shows today's date.
You're correct. Let me call the duty manager before we discuss alternatives.
The breakfast charge appeared even though we booked room only.
Did you visit the restaurant this morning?
Only to meet our friends. We didn't order anything.
I'll check with the restaurant and remove any charge made in error.
We asked for a quiet room because my partner works nights.
The room you've been given is quiet after the restaurant closes.
She needs to sleep during the day, though.
I see. A room above the garden would suit you better.
I'd like late checkout, but I don't need the room cleaned.
The main issue is preparing it for the next guest.
Could we leave our bags somewhere and just use the lounge?
Absolutely. That option won't require extending your room booking.
I returned the borrowed charger, but the deposit hasn't appeared.
Was the deposit taken in cash or held on your card?
It was a card hold when we checked in.
I'll give you written confirmation that we've released it.
One of my shirts came back from the laundry with a mark.
Do you still have the laundry receipt?
Yes, and I took a photo before sending it down.
Please leave the shirt with reception so the laundry team can investigate.
We booked a family room, and one person can no longer come.
Would you like to change rooms or keep the space?
Keep the room, but can the extra breakfast be removed?
Yes. The room rate stays the same, but breakfast is charged separately.
My key stopped working after I kept it beside my phone.
Sometimes the card needs to be reset.
Could you check it before issuing another one?
Of course. I'll also confirm that the checkout date is correct.
The bill includes a minibar item we didn't use.
Which item is listed?
A bottle of juice. We only drank the tap water.
I'll ask housekeeping to check the stock record.
I almost gave the hotel a poor review because of the building work.
Was the noise a problem throughout your stay?
Only on the first day, and the staff moved us promptly.
Then mentioning both the problem and the response would give a fairer picture.
shopping: I'm looking for a shirt I can wear to work without ironing it every morning.
This fabric creases less, but it feels slightly warmer.
Can I try it under the jacket I usually wear?
Certainly. Comfort matters more than how it looks on the hanger.
I'd like to exchange these shoes, although I've worn them indoors.
Was that just to check the fit?
Yes. After ten minutes I realised they pressed against my heel.
Let us inspect the soles and discuss a size that might work better.
The advertised discount makes this seem cheaper than the smaller pack.
Have you compared the price per item?
Not yet. The large label distracted me.
The shelf has both figures. The smaller pack is actually better value today.
The replacement headphones have developed the same fault as the first pair.
Do you have the record of the earlier exchange?
Yes. I don't want to keep replacing the same model.
We'll look at the full history before offering the next step.
I received a collection message, but the shop says the parcel hasn't arrived.
The message might have been sent when it reached the local depot.
It specifically says ready to collect, though.
Then you shouldn't have made the journey. I'll check where the scan happened.
I sent a gift directly to my friend, and she received the price invoice.
Did you select the gift option at checkout?
I did. I kept a screenshot because it was her birthday.
Please send that to us so we can find out what went wrong.
Your voucher says ten pounds off, but I only saved three.
The discount stops when the order reaches the minimum spend.
That condition wasn't visible on the offer page.
I'll compare the page with the full terms before answering you.
The used bicycle is cheaper, but it needs a new chain soon.
Has the shop included that in the asking price?
They reduced it a little after showing me the inspection sheet.
Then compare the total repair cost with a bike that's ready to ride.
Why are you putting the item in another box? It already has one.
The outer box protects it during delivery.
I'm collecting it on foot, so I won't need that.
In that case, we can leave the extra packaging here.
I've pre-ordered the book twice because the first payment looked unsuccessful.
Do you have two confirmation numbers?
Yes, and both payments now appear on my statement.
Don't place another order. We'll identify and cancel the duplicate.
home: The cleaning rota looks equal, but the bathroom takes much longer than the hall.
I hadn't thought about the time involved.
Could we swap jobs each week instead of keeping the same ones?
That would let everyone see how much work each job needs.
The plumber repaired the tap, but the cupboard underneath is still damp.
Did anyone check the pipe behind the washing machine?
No. We assumed the tap was the only source.
Let's record where the water appears before arranging another visit.
I lent my ladder to someone and now a step is bent.
Have they told you what happened?
They said it was already like that, but I used it yesterday.
I'd stop using it and speak to them before lending anything else.
The delivery driver left my parcel with a neighbour who is away.
Do you know when they're coming back?
Not for another week, and I need the contents for work.
Contact the delivery company with the photo rather than trying to enter the property.
My neighbour's washing machine runs against our bedroom wall every night.
Have you told them when you hear it?
I mentioned the noise, but not the time.
A specific example may help them understand what needs to change.
The person applying for our spare room works from home all week.
Would that be a problem for the shared space?
Only if they expect the kitchen table to be their desk.
Then discuss working arrangements before agreeing to the tenancy.
We packed the things we'll need first at the bottom of the van.
Is there a way to unload them separately?
Not easily. The bedding is behind every piece of furniture.
Next time we'll label an essentials box and keep it with us.
The new washing machine uses less energy, yet our bills haven't fallen.
Are we doing the same number of washes?
Probably more, because the new one is so convenient.
The lower cost per wash doesn't mean the total use has dropped.
The rent increase is small, but the new agreement removes our parking space.
Was the parking included in the original contract?
Yes. I nearly signed because I only checked the monthly amount.
It's worth comparing the whole agreement, not just the price.
Our cat hid from the neighbour and missed two meals while we were away.
Did the neighbour stay long enough for her to come out?
She visited at the agreed times, but left quickly.
We need a plan that suits the animal, not just a list of feeding times.
health: I booked the first available appointment, then realised I couldn't get there by bus.
Did the system show the location before you confirmed?
Yes, but I didn't know it was the branch outside town.
Ask about the nearer branch instead of simply missing the appointment.
The exercise class is described as suitable for everyone.
Did you find that accurate?
Most exercises were done on the floor, which didn't work for me.
Tell the organiser which part was difficult so they can explain the available options.
I keep saying yes to evening commitments because I don't want to disappoint people.
Then you end up cancelling when you're exhausted?
Exactly. It makes me feel less reliable, not more.
Perhaps deciding earlier would be kinder to everyone involved.
The restaurant gave us an allergy menu from last season.
Did they confirm whether the dishes have changed?
They said probably not, which wasn't reassuring.
Ask them to check the current information rather than rely on the old sheet.
Our walking group wants to move faster, but two members would be left behind.
Could you have two groups following different routes?
We'd need another leader, but both routes could end together.
That sounds more welcoming than asking people to keep up at any cost.
The refill point is free, yet almost nobody uses it.
Is it easy to find from the main entrance?
Not really. The sign is behind a tall display.
Move the sign before assuming people prefer bottled water.
My calendar has a break at lunchtime, but colleagues keep booking over it.
Do they see that time as available?
The calendar says tentative, so perhaps they do.
Make the status clear and explain when you can take their calls.
The replacement class costs more because it's run by a different instructor.
Was an extra charge mentioned when the first class was cancelled?
No. We were told our bookings would transfer.
Then the organiser needs to explain the change before taking any payment.
I've stopped recording my progress because I keep missing the target.
Does the target still reflect the time you actually have?
No, it was based on a quiet week last month.
You could review the target without treating that as a failure.
The sports centre improved the main entrance but left the changing area unchanged.
Did they ask users to test the whole route?
They only checked whether people could enter the building.
Access needs to work for the visit, not just the front door.
study: The library has the book, but only as a reference copy.
Can you use it in the reading room?
Yes, though I can't stay during the library's usual hours.
Ask whether another edition is available to borrow before buying one.
I answered the homework question, but I lost marks for the method.
Were you asked to show each stage?
Apparently, but I only wrote the final answer.
Ask which steps demonstrate understanding rather than just adding more writing.
We spend so much time organising our study group that we rarely study.
How many people have to agree on each session?
All twelve. Even choosing a chapter becomes a discussion.
Try setting a regular time and letting people join when they can.
My extension was approved, but the submission system still shows the old deadline.
Have you saved the approval message?
Yes. I'm worried an automatic late penalty will appear.
Send the message to the course office while there's still time to correct it.
The teacher's feedback says my argument is clear but not supported.
Does each paragraph include evidence?
I mostly explain what I think, then repeat it in the conclusion.
Choose one claim and show how a source or example supports it.
This course promises advanced conversation, but the sample lesson looks quite basic.
Have you asked who the course is intended for?
They said anyone who wants to improve.
Request the actual level requirements before paying for a place.
I can give my presentation from memory until someone interrupts.
Have you practised answering questions during it?
No. I always rehearse from the first sentence to the last.
Try starting from different points so one interruption doesn't break the whole sequence.
The recording of our online lesson has no captions.
Did anyone request them before the course began?
Yes, and the course page said recordings would be accessible.
Keep that information when you ask the provider to resolve it.
Two websites quote the same statistic, but neither links to the research.
Maybe they copied it from each other.
That's what I suspect. The number looks unusually exact.
Trace the earliest source rather than treating repeated claims as separate evidence.
I can recognise every term in my notes, but I struggle to explain them.
Have you tried closing the notes and teaching one idea to someone?
Not yet. Reading everything again feels safer.
That might show you which parts you understand and which only look familiar.
work: Our meeting has sixteen people, although only three need to make the decision.
Could the others send updates beforehand?
Probably. Most just read out information from the shared document.
Then separate the updates from the discussion that actually needs everyone.
I keep receiving new tasks because I finish the earlier ones quickly.
Have you explained what you're already responsible for?
I usually say yes and catch up after hours.
Make the workload visible before people assume you have spare capacity.
The remote-working trial went well, but management wants everyone back full-time.
Have they explained which problems returning would solve?
They mainly say that collaboration happens naturally in person.
It may help to compare specific examples from the trial rather than argue in general terms.
The guide tells new staff to ask a colleague whenever they're unsure.
That sounds reasonable, but what happens when the colleague is wrong?
Different people teach the same task in different ways.
We need one agreed process that people can check, not just informal advice.
We can meet the deadline if we leave out the testing.
Would the customer know the difference before using it?
Probably not, which makes the shortcut tempting.
Then we need to explain the risk instead of calling an untested delivery finished.
The new starter is friendly, but nobody has explained who decides what.
Has the induction covered roles as well as systems?
Mostly passwords, forms and where to find the printer.
Arrange a few short introductions around the work they'll actually be doing.
I thought my colleague rejected my idea, but she was questioning the budget.
Did you ask which part she disagreed with?
No. I started defending the whole proposal.
Clarifying the objection first could save both of you a difficult conversation.
The report is accurate, but readers can't tell which figures have changed.
Could we highlight the changes instead of making them compare two long files?
Yes. We already have the earlier version.
Add a short explanation as well, so the reason for each change is clear.
Our suggestion scheme gets plenty of ideas, but nobody hears what happens next.
Do the people submitting them get a reply?
Only an automatic thank-you message.
Even a reason for not proceeding would show that someone has considered the proposal.
I'm taking over a project with dozens of messages but no decision record.
Can the previous lead give you a short handover call?
She's available tomorrow, though only for half an hour.
Use that time to identify the decisions and open questions rather than read every message.
technology: Our team shares one login because it's easier than creating separate accounts.
Does that make it difficult to see who changed a document?
Yes. Last week we couldn't trace an accidental deletion.
Convenience is costing us accountability. Let's ask about individual access.
The client could view the draft yesterday, but today the link is blocked.
Was the file moved into a different folder?
Yes. I didn't realise that would affect the permissions.
Check the new folder's rules before sending another link.
We have a backup drive, but nobody has tried restoring a file from it.
Is it even clear which folders are included?
Not since we reorganised the shared space.
A successful backup message isn't enough. We should test a small restore.
I muted the work chat, then missed a genuinely urgent message.
Could urgent issues use a different channel?
We never agreed what counts as urgent.
That's the conversation to have before turning every notification back on.
The update solved a bug, but removed a feature our team relied on.
Was the removal mentioned in the release notes?
It was, buried near the bottom.
We should check important changes before rolling future updates out to everyone.
Support asked me to restart the router for the third time.
Have you given them a record of when the connection drops?
I've described it, but I haven't kept times.
A short log might help move the investigation beyond the standard checklist.
The app says my data is anonymous, yet it still asks for my exact location.
Does it explain why that level of detail is needed?
Only that it improves the service.
That's too general. I'd look for a clearer explanation before enabling it.
The new website works with bigger text until the payment screen.
What happens there?
Two buttons overlap, and I can't tell which one is selected.
Include that step in the report. The earlier pages alone don't show the problem.
The assistant produced a convincing answer with a reference that doesn't exist.
Did anyone check it before putting it in the report?
Luckily, one person searched for the source.
We need that check built into the process, not left to whoever happens to notice.
I thought I'd cancelled, but I had only turned off the reminder emails.
Was the cancellation option labelled clearly?
Not at all. It was several screens away.
Save the confirmation once you finish, so there's no doubt about what changed.
environment: The recycling rate has fallen since the new bins arrived.
Are residents confused by the colours?
Possibly. The colours mean something different in the neighbouring town.
Use labels with examples instead of expecting everyone to know the local system.
The council installed a water-saving tap, but it now runs for too long.
Has anyone reported the actual fault?
The maintenance request just says the new tap is unpopular.
Describe the problem precisely so it reaches the right team.
The school planted trees for an event, but several died over the summer.
Was anyone responsible for watering them during the holidays?
Each group assumed another group was doing it.
The next planting plan needs a maintenance plan too.
Volunteers spent the morning collecting litter, then left full bags beside the river.
Was a collection arranged?
They expected the usual waste service to take them.
We should confirm the final step before inviting people to do the first one.
The community market wants more local sellers but has raised the stall fee.
Is the increase covering a specific new cost?
Mostly advertising outside the area.
Then ask whether that spending helps the small sellers the market wants to attract.
The tool-sharing project is busy, but the same two people repair everything.
Do users know how much time maintenance takes?
They only see the borrowing calendar.
Show the work behind the service and invite people to share it.
People keep saying reusable cups are always the greener choice.
Does that include how often they're used and washed?
Nobody has measured that here.
Let's find out about our actual use before printing a confident claim.
The cycle lane is protected except for the busiest part of the road.
Why was that section left out?
It would remove a few parking spaces.
Then the safety claim needs to be weighed against the route people really have to take.
Our public meeting was well attended, but only five people spoke.
Were there other ways to give feedback?
No, and several people left before questions began.
Offer a quieter way to contribute rather than assuming silence means agreement.
The winning project has the most supporters online, but serves only one street.
Was the grant meant to reward popularity or wider benefit?
The rules never made that clear.
We should settle the criteria before asking residents to vote again.
